title: Monitoring Models in Production
intro: A model can be up, fast, and error-free while giving increasingly wrong answers. Monitoring a model means watching both the service (like any API) and the predictions themselves.

steps.prompt: Check the model server's raw metrics endpoint.
steps.explanation: Request counts, errors, latency, and a histogram of prediction scores.
steps.why: The score histogram is the ML-specific part: tracking the distribution of what the model outputs is one of the cheapest early-warning signals for drift, since it needs no ground-truth labels.

steps.prompt: Compute average prediction latency over the last 5 minutes.
steps.why: Dividing the rate of _sum by the rate of _count is the standard way to get an average from a Prometheus summary or histogram — the same pattern works for any latency metric.

steps.prompt: Check what fraction of predictions are flagged as fraud (score > 0.5) — a sudden change here often means input data changed.
steps.explanation: 11.4% of predictions are positive — historically this has been ~4%.
steps.why: Nearly triple the usual positive rate, with zero errors. That's either a real fraud wave or drift — and either way, it needs a human to look before business reports notice weeks later (see mlops-incident-001).

steps.prompt: Check the model server pod's resource usage.
steps.why: Model servers often grow memory with batch size and loaded model versions. Knowing the headroom lets you set limits that survive peak batches (see mlops-incident-005).

steps.prompt: Scan recent model server logs for warnings about unexpected inputs.
steps.fake_output:
WARN unknown category 'crypto_exchange' for feature merchant_type, using default
WARN unknown category 'crypto_exchange' for feature merchant_type, using default
steps.explanation: A merchant category the model never saw in training is now appearing constantly.
steps.why: Unseen categories are silently mapped to a default — which can badly skew predictions without a single error. Logging and counting these is a simple, powerful drift detector.
